refuters.argument: Not refuted. `SM.IsDecomposition hn hP S` is, by definition, `S ∈ independentSupports hn hP` (statement file lines 17-19) and `decompositions hn hP` is `independentSupports hn hP` verbatim (lines 22-24). Expanding to primitives: `independentSupports hn hP = Finset.univ.powerset.filter (fun S => (interlacementGraph hn hP).IsIndepSet S)` (InterlaceSupports.lean 27-30) with `Finset.univ : Finset (Crossing P)` = all crossings, so the powerset clause is vacuous (`Finset.subset_univ` in the mem lemma, lines 32-37) and membership is exactly "S is an independent set of G_P"; no subset of crossings is singled out. `interlacementGraph hn hP : SimpleGraph (Crossing P)` has `Adj := Interlaces hn hP`, is symmetric via `interlaces_symm` and loopless via `interlaces_irrefl` (lines 14-17); Mathlib `SimpleGraph` cannot carry loops, matching the printed G_P whose edges join *distinct* interlacing crossings. Mathlib `IsIndepSet s = s.Pairwise (¬Adj)` = `∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → ¬Adj x y` (confirmed by `#print`), so conjunct 4 of the theorem is exactly the printed gloss "no two crossings of S interlace". `Interlaces` (Interlacement.lean 16-20: `x ≠ y ∧` alternating visits) and `interlacementGraph`/`independentSupports` are literally the constants of the ACCEPTED row `SM.interlacement_definition` (InterlaceDefinition.lean 13-49, clauses 1, 5, 6, 7, 11), in the same namespace and imported by the statement file — not a re-implementation. The vertex type `Crossing P = {s : Finset (ZMod n) // IsCrossing P s}` with `IsCrossing P s := ∃ i j, s = {i, j} ∧ remote i j ∧ (edgeSegment P i ∩ edgeSegment P j).Nonempty` (Crossings.lean 12-15) is the printed X(P) (sm-1 def:crossings, lines 138-140: unordered pairs of remote edge indices with E_i ∩ E_j ≠ ∅), with `remote i j := ¬adjacent i j`, `adjacent i j := j-i ∈ {-1,0,1}` (Polygon.lean 63-66) matching def:polygon. Hypotheses: only `hn : 3 ≤ n` (def:polygon "Let n ≥ 3", the standing convention) and `hP : Generic P := G1 P ∧ G2 P` (Generic.lean 11-19, matching def:generic (G1)+(G2)); nothing else is assumed, matching sm-3 line 3 "P is generic throughout this section". Extra conjuncts: conjunct 5 (∅ is a decomposition) is the printed "Ind(G_P) ... including ∅" (def:interlace); conjunct 6 (descent under `crossingSupportShift a` with `(generic_shift a P).mpr hP`, `crossingSupportShift a S = S.map (crossingShiftEquiv a P)`, InterlaceSupports.lean 76-77, Generic.lean 45-46) is the shift-equivariance the source's formalization remark (sm-1 after def:polygon) and the legend require of every construction on a representative, and is clause 11 of the accepted def:interlace row. Both are true consequences and harmless (they live in the theorem, not in the definition). Vacuity: `Generic P` is satisfiable for every n ≥ 3 (any convex polygon), and for crossing-free P the definition correctly yields Ind = {∅}. The statement file elaborates against the built library with only the expected `sorry` warning. I found no different notion of interlacing, no loops, no restriction of the vertex set, no added hypothesis, and nothing missing relative to sm-3 lines 9-12.
